The evidence

From input to outcome

Each record names the skill, shows what it received and did, and points to the result or source. All purchase examples use synthetic data.

Business solution skill

Debit Card Fraud Demo Builder

Builds an explainable, synthetic debit-card fraud demonstration that scores transactions, routes uncertain purchases to verification, and reports fraud and false-decline outcomes.

  1. Input

    A synthetic CSV transaction with purchase amount, recent average, merchant and device status, location, velocity, travel notice, customer verification response, and an evaluation-only fraud label.

  2. Interaction

    The skill validates the row, creates explainable risk signals, and calculates a bounded 0–100 demo score. It assigns APPROVE (0–39), VERIFY (40–79), or DECLINE (80–100); VERIFY uses the customer’s YES or NO response to set the final action.

  3. Resulting change

    The demo shows the score, initial and final actions, reason codes, and a plain-English explanation, then rolls synthetic outcomes into fraud recall, false-decline rate, fraud dollars prevented, and legitimate dollars preserved.

Source trail

The demo builder defines the scoring rules, verification flow, metrics, test cases, and guardrails. It requires synthetic or de-identified data and explicitly limits the work to demonstrations and prototypes.

Evidence

▣ Demonstration output

The skill produces a synthetic transaction simulator, customer-verification flow, dashboard metrics, scenario controls, and scoring checks without using real cardholder data.

UX and design skill

Frontend Design Premium

Makes the evidence readable and easy to inspect across desktop, narrow windows, and mobile.

  1. Input

    The Evidence page used a five-column table for three distinct roles. Its cells became a long, repetitive stack on small screens.

  2. Interaction

    The design review called for a quick role index and a consistent input → interaction → resulting change sequence for each skill, with source details kept alongside the claim.

  3. Resulting change

    This page now uses three evidence records. The sequence stays visible as columns on wide screens and reflows into one readable column on phones.

Source trail

The revised Evidence page is the design output. It retains the Northstar colors and navigation while replacing the table layout.

Testing and quality skill

Playwright

Automates a real browser to test page behavior and layouts at different screen sizes.

  1. Input

    The Evidence page at 1280, 800, 390, and 320 pixel widths, plus role links and the mobile menu.

  2. Interaction

    Playwright opened the local page, checked for horizontal overflow and page errors, followed a role link, and opened the mobile menu.

  3. Resulting change

    All three records rendered, none of the checked widths overflowed, the role link and menu worked, and the browser reported no page errors.

Source trail

These are local browser checks of the Evidence page. They do not measure the accuracy of a production fraud system.
